name: Microsoft Fabric for BI developers
tagline: OneLake, Lakehouse vs Warehouse, the SQL analytics endpoint, Direct Lake on OneLake vs on SQL, framing and fallback, Dataflow Gen2, mirroring and medallion design.
seo: Microsoft Fabric practice for Power BI developers: OneLake, Lakehouse, Warehouse, SQL analytics endpoint, shortcuts, Direct Lake on OneLake vs Direct Lake on SQL endpoint, framing, fallback, guardrails, Dataflow Gen2, mirroring and medallion architecture. Verified against current Microsoft documentation.
intro: Fabric changes where data preparation happens and how semantic models read data. This track focuses on the decisions a BI developer makes in Fabric, not every Fabric workload. Fabric features change fast: each topic shows when it was last checked against Microsoft's documentation, and the CI flags it when a review is due. A Fabric trial covers every hands-on step; where you can't use one, the conceptual tasks and the Sprint 09 decision still apply.
setup: A Fabric trial (or capacity) and a workspace you own. Upload the company pack CSVs to a lakehouse. No Spark knowledge is required: everything can be done with the UI, Dataflow Gen2 and T-SQL.
